skill.name: hook-development
skill.description: Guides developers through designing, configuring, testing, and migrating Claude Code hooks for validation, automation, and workflow enforcement.
skill.summary: Build safer Claude Code hooks for validation, automation, and workflow control.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, or defensive hook examples. Confirmed issues remain in the local hook test helper and in examples that persist raw hook payloads. No prompt-injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: Command injection in the hook testing helper.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid bash -c with user-controlled hook paths. Validate the path, quote it, and execute the hook without shell string interpolation.

remediation.issue: Raw hook payloads are logged to persistent destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Log only minimal fields. Redact prompts, file content, credentials, command output, and other sensitive hook input before storage.

remediation.issue: Database logging example builds SQL with raw hook input.
remediation.suggestion: Use parameterized queries or a logging API instead of interpolating hook input into a psql command string.

remediation.issue: Shell examples build JSON output through string concatenation.
remediation.suggestion: Generate hook responses with jq or another JSON encoder so paths and messages are escaped correctly.

remediation.issue: Temporary state examples use predictable files under /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp, private directories, strict permissions, and cleanup handlers for hook state and cache files.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable hooks to validate tool use and enforce workflow rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users through hook design, testing, and migration patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Claude Code hook events, matchers, inputs, outputs, and exit behavior.
Compares prompt-based hooks with command hooks for common validation tasks.
Provides examples for Bash validation, file write checks, and SessionStart context loading.
Includes utility scripts for hook schema validation, hook testing, and shell linting.
Covers migration from basic command hooks to prompt-based hook workflows.
Documents lifecycle limits, timeout choices, and plugin-relative path conventions.
limitations: It does not replace official Claude Code documentation for version-specific behavior.
Example shell scripts require local review before production deployment.
Some examples depend on tools such as bash, jq, timeout, psql, or curl.
Hook configuration changes usually require restarting Claude Code.

use_cases.title: Add File Safety Hooks
use_cases.description: Create PreToolUse hooks that review write paths, sensitive files, and path traversal before tools run.

use_cases.title: Enforce Workflow Completion
use_cases.description: Design Stop hooks that check tests, builds, and unanswered questions before an agent ends work.

use_cases.title: Migrate Hook Logic
use_cases.description: Move brittle shell checks into prompt-based hooks while keeping fast deterministic checks where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for file write validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PreToolUse hook for Write and Edit. It should block system paths, credential files, and path traversal.

prompt_templates.title: Add Session Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for project-specific environment context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SessionStart hook that detects my project type. Store only safe environment values for later hooks.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Bash Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from command hooks to prompt hooks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing command hook. Recommend which checks should become prompt-based and which checks should stay deterministic.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Hook Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hook strategy for my plugin. Include PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, testing steps, and safe logging rules.

output_examples.input: User asks to add a hook that blocks unsafe file writes.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a PreToolUse design with matcher choices, safety criteria, timeout guidance, and test steps.

output_examples.input: User shares an existing Bash validation hook.
output_examples.output: The skill provides a migration plan that separates fast shell checks from contextual prompt-based decisions.

output_examples.input: User wants to test hooks before release.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests schema validation, sample inputs, debug mode checks, and linter review before deployment.

best_practices: Prefer prompt-based hooks for contextual decisions and command hooks for fast deterministic checks.
Validate and quote all command hook inputs before using paths, commands, or environment values.
Test hooks with sample inputs, schema validation, debug mode, and failure cases before deployment.
anti_patterns: Trusting raw tool input without validation or JSON escaping.
Logging complete hook payloads to external systems or persistent audit files.
Depending on hook execution order or expecting current sessions to reload changed hooks.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code hooks that validate tool use, load context, enforce policies, and test hook behavior.

faq.question: Does it support prompt-based hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on prompt-based hooks for PreToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, and UserPromptSubmit workflows.

faq.question: Can I still use command hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains command hooks for deterministic checks, external tools, and performance-sensitive logic.

faq.question: Does it include runnable examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes example shell hooks and utility scripts, but they require local security review before production use.

faq.question: Will hook edits apply immediately?
faq.answer: Usually no. Claude Code loads hook configuration at session start, so changes normally require a restart.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The hook concepts are for Claude Code plugins. The marketplace metadata also helps Claude and Codex users find it.
